what: What the design site's Vehicles review page shows for this car (R126). tools/vehicles/review/build.mjs turns this, vehicle.json, the bake and assets/profiles/<id>.json into art/ui/poc/vehicles/<id>/; tools/vehicles/review/check.mjs fails if any Vehicles-contract item is missing. Paths are repo-relative.
name: Pig Catcher
summary: R123's Pig Catcher: a bubbly outback trail bike in the spirit of the DR-Z400E (no Suzuki branding): tall long-travel forks, a beaked front mudguard, wide plastics, a light bar with two spotlights, and a rear rack carrying a coiled rope and a hessian sack. The rider is part of the model, standing on the pegs in a green MX helmet, khaki shirt and jeans. Code-built from a generated reference sheet (R81), on the bike part set (core, front, back, rider, wheel_F, wheel_R).
feedback: Comment on this page (what to change, which view or state); the session turns each comment into a bug bead that cites this page and the car's id.

reference.note: The reference sheets were generated with Muse Image from a written brief (art/vehicles/pig-catcher/refs/prompts/), the Cruz Missile's sheet given as the layout example. Per view: the reference crop, the model shaded, and the silhouette diff (green is model only, red is reference only). Scored by tools/vehicles/fit (Spike J's method: perspective camera, the same mask pipeline on both sides, the contact-shadow band left out). Bikes are thin: the masks keep pale parts (segment.bright), use a small opening and keep detached components (refs/sheets.json), the same rules on both sides.

damage.note: Left to right: intact; front and back loose; the rider loose; wheel_F cambered; front detached; the rider thrown (detached, R121); back detached; wheel_F detached; rider and front detached; a stripped frame. Posed in a three.js viewer about each part's hinge line (tools/vehicles/evidence).

paints.pattern: Seat colour on the paint key (the plastics, tank and mudguards tint); the black light bar, the rope, the sack and the rider keep their colours. The number sits on the rider's back (anchor roof_number) and in the HUD badge.
